native_result.query: The effect of which variable on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636 to -0.2293 (while becoming insignifcant) when both race and academic characteristics are included in analysis?
native_result.HypoA: The effect of SES on BA degree completion decreases from 0.3636  (significant) to  -0.2293 (insignificant) and effect of race on BA degree completion decreases from 0.5024  (significant) to 0.0923 (insignificant) when academic characteristics are considered.
native_result.HypoB: SES (socioeconomic status) is the variable whose effect on BA degree completion decreases from ~0.3636 to ~-0.2293 and loses significance when race and academic characteristics (ASVAB composite score and class percentile) are added. In nested logistic regressions on n=8,773 (BA completion rate 2.7%), the SES log-odds coefficient falls from +0.3548 (se=0.088, p<0.001, OR=1.43; race-only base: +0.3524; cloglog: +0.3471) to -0.2379 (se=0.101, p=0.018, OR=0.79; cloglog: -0.2290 ≈ target -0.2293) once academic measures enter; it is insignificant at the 1% level (robust-SE p≈0.033), and in the linear probability model with family size included it flips to -0.0013 and is clearly insignificant (p=0.66). The apparent positive SES gradient is mediated by academic resources: SES correlates 0.46 with the ASVAB composite and 0.30 with class percentile, and conditional on measured academic performance, higher-SES students are no more (if anything slightly less) likely to complete a BA. Including family size reverses the flip (SES stays +0.29), so family size is a key suppressor; no other variable (sex, family size, race dummies) matches the 0.3636→-0.2293 sign-flip-and-loss-of-significance pattern across any tested specification.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Data audit: 8,773 rows x 8 cols, zero missing; BA=236 events (2.7%); race 3-category; SES standardized; verified no duplicate CASE IDs. 2) Nested models: logit with base (SES+sex+race dummies, White ref) vs full (+ASVAB composite + class percentile), plus average marginal effects; LPM (HC1) as robustness. 3) Systematic replication grid: {logit, probit, cloglog, LPM} x covariate sets (race/sex/family size in/out) x SES raw/standardized x percentile raw/reversed x classical/HC0-HC3 SEs, searching for the 0.3636→-0.2293 path (best match: logit, raw SES, family size excluded; 27 specifications stored in CSV). 4) Diagnostics: ASVAB-percentile correlation 0.70 but all VIFs <2.7; M2 logit converged with no separation (fitted probabilities 0.0003-0.47); flip scan of every candidate variable; percentile-coding sensitivity check (reversal flips only the percentile's own coefficient, leaving SES unchanged).

evaluator_config.judge_settings_policy: Native per-call settings are forwarded to the configured Judge; incompatible providers must reject rather than ignore them.
adaptations: Injected independent judge instead of hardcoded OpenAI client.
Malformed judge output raises an evaluation error; no hidden retries.
evaluator_config.aggregation: recall_context * mean_accuracy_score; unmatched predicted contexts stay in denominator
evaluator_config.native_behavior_preserved: Variable/relation comparisons receive full hypotheses for each matched context pair.
